Low Tide

M. Halloran
The sea goes out the way a thought goes out,
not all at once, but leaving things behind:
a rope, a shell, the outline of a doubt
still glistening where the water was resigned.
I walk the flats it gave me for an hour
and count the bright and temporary land,
then feel it turning, slow as any power,
and the cold returning, grain by grain of sand.
